title: Traffic surge & fallback onboarding screens for version routing
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Scope: Design a compact quickstart onboarding flow and a set of annotated product screenshots that teach engineers and platform owners how to use version routing: canary rollouts, A/B splits, and traffic-based fallback policies when capacity or health degrades. Deliverables: 1) 6-screen onboarding microflow for the Console Quickstart modal; 2) 3 hero product screenshots (canary panel, A/B split editor, fallback rules editor) with callouts and microcopy; 3) an accessibility checklist and alt-text for each asset; 4) shareable doc + Figma file links; 5) edge-case guidance for traffic surges and automated rollback scenarios.
assets: Example screenshot PNGs: canary_panel_v2.png, ab_split_editor_v3.png, fallback_rules_flow_v1.png
microcopy: Welcome modal headline: 'Rollouts made predictable — route traffic by version, safely.'
A/B split label: 'Traffic distribution — primary vs variant(s)'
Fallback suggestion: 'Enable health-based fallback: instantly divert traffic to stable model when errors spike.'
Tooltip for pinning: 'Pin this route to model v1.3 to avoid automatic upgrades.'
ux_notes: Design should prioritize compact, scannable steps for 1-minute setup; assume user is an engineer familiar with models.
Include keyboard-focus states and aria-labels for all interactive controls (sliders, toggles, dropdowns).
Show contextual risk-level banners (Low/Medium/High) based on chosen split and fallback settings.
Fallback rules editor should visualize live traffic paths: primary -> variant -> fallback. Use color-blind friendly palette.
When showing canary creation, surface recommended defaults (5% traffic, 30m evaluation window) with quick links to advanced options.
